Maya (runtime): Heads up — token/sec on hosted-canary-3 dropped ~40% after yesterday's runtime merge rtdiff@1267. Repro'ing on canary. Looks like continuous-batcher queueing + kernel choice interaction. Anyone watching?
Sam (oncall): Which canary pool exactly? eu-west?
Maya (runtime): hosted-canary-3 (ctb pool). Logs show batches queueing ~200-400ms and then a kernel fallback to gemm32 at around t=0.6s that coincides with the drop.
Raghu (profiling): CI perf also flagged a regression on the ctb_throughput job — ~9% token/sec loss on candidate vs baseline. I have a perf flame but can't attach here. Quick CI numbers: baseline 12.3k tok/s -> candidate 11.2k tok/s. p95 latency +120ms. :eyes:
CI Bot: Perf report: suite=c/tb_throughput seed=42 baseline_tok_s=12345 candidate_tok_s=11200 regression=9.2% p95_increase_ms=120
Maya (runtime): I started a local bisect: narrowed to merge 1267e9bbe — kernel-policy change that added a fallback path for small-batch GEMM when memcopy heuristics trigger. Reverting that commit locally restores throughput.
Lena (scheduler): If kernel fallback happens while queue depth > 2 it can amplify latency because next batches switch execution path and kv-cache warmup misses. Maybe the policy should consult queue depth before allowing fallback.
Raghu (profiling): Profiling snippet (short):
```
kv_cache: miss_rate before=6% after=29%  # correlates with tok/sec drop
batcher: avg_wait_ms baseline=18 candidate=62
kernel: selected=fast_conv -> fallback=gemm32 at t=0.6s
memcopy: memcpy_bytes/sec spike coincident with fallback
```
Sam (oncall): Can we try a targeted rollback (kernel policy revert) and run quick canary? I don't want to change batching quantum yet.
Maya (runtime): I'm opening a rollback PR now and will run canary build. Marking rollout as hold until we validate.
Maya (runtime): PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1428 (WIP) — revert kernel-policy change in 1267e9bbe.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for hosted-canary-3. Reason: performance_regression_detected (token/sec drop).
Lena (scheduler): In parallel I can add a safety gate: disallow kernel fallback when batcher.queue_depth >= 3 and kv_cache.miss_rate elevated. That should be low-risk fallback guard.
Raghu (profiling): Agree. Also add a micro-benchmark patch to the CI perf suite that exercises small batches + cache-warmup to catch this class of regressions in PRs.
Sam (oncall): Running rollback canary now — will post numbers in ~10m.
Maya (runtime): Thanks. If rollback fixes it we'll ship revert and then iterate on a safer policy. Will follow up with perf artifacts and a short postmortem.
